transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia, I'll run the call, Marcus from our SE team is here as well. quick intro?
[00:08] Dr. Priya Raman (Zenwell): Priya here, head of ML. we own model infra and evaluation.
[00:12] Tom Alvarez (Zenwell): Tom, eng manager, will be point on infra and data.
[00:16] Linda Park (Zenwell): Linda, compliance. I'll flag anything security / SOC 2 related.
[00:20] Marcus Lee (Redwood SE): Hi all, Marcus. I'll handle technical details and benchmarking.
[00:25] Sofia: Goal for today - scope the POC quality eval plan: what are your success criteria, how big is the workload, what benchmarks we run, timelines. we'll also cover golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, and how we score.
[00:37] Tom: high level - we want to validate that Redwood's hosted or dedicated runtime can meet our latency and hallucination thresholds for the summarization and triage assistant we run. also want to see consistent output format for downstream ingestion.
[00:46] Priya: success criteria from ML: at least 90% pass on golden prompts, hallucination rate <2% on clinical facts, and format conformance 99% for JSON schema. latency p95 target depends on deployment: hosted we can accept p95 < 600ms, dedicated we want p95 < 350ms.
[01:05] Marcus: ok noted. we'll design the eval to run both hosted and dedicated variants where possible. we usually recommend a 4-week pilot: week 0 setup, week 1 baseline perf, week 2 quality + regression, week 3 final analysis and tuning. is that aligned?
[01:20] Tom: that sounds reasonable. question — sample volume: we process ~10k requests/day in staging, peak 25k/day. for POC do you need full volume?
[01:29] Marcus: for baseline perf we want to run scaled load tests to reach representative qps, but the quality eval itself uses a curated set: 200-500 golden prompts plus a 1k random sample for regression. for hallucination checks, we'll seed with 150 clinical-fact prompts that have known ground truth.
[01:44] Sofia: can you confirm acceptable acceptance thresholds again for the internal stakeholders?
[01:48] Priya: yes — golden prompt pass rate >=90%, regression F1 drop <3% vs our on-prem model baseline, hallucination rate <2% when measured by entity hallucination metric, and structural/format errors <1%. also latency SLOs as I mentioned.
[02:05] Marcus: good. scoring approach we propose: weighted composite score — Accuracy (50%), Format conformance (20%), Hallucination penalty (20% negative weight), Latency (10%). we compute per-prompt scoring and aggregate. we'll share the scoring script as a Jupyter notebook.
[02:26] Tom: for hallucination penalty, can you clarify how negative weight works?
[02:30] Marcus: yeah so if a prompt is flagged for hallucination, it reduces the accuracy score for that prompt and we count it as a hard failure for golden prompts. For the composite score we cap negative impact to avoid one-off noisy items dominating.
[02:43] Priya: can you give an example?
[02:45] Marcus: e.g., a golden prompt that expects a treatment name; model returns a fabricated drug -> that prompt gets 0 for accuracy, adds a hallucination flag; overall composite drops accordingly.
[02:54] Sofia: let's talk golden prompts — Tom, can you confirm you'll provide 200 curated golden prompts covering edge cases, privacy-sensitive cases, and common templates?
[03:03] Tom: yes we'll aim for 200; at least 50 should be edge cases and 30 should be privacy redaction tests.
[03:10] Linda: we also need to include prompts that test PHI handling, ensure no leaked identifiers. how will you check that?
[03:16] Marcus: we'll run redaction detection in the evaluation pipeline and include rules for PII/PHI pattern matches plus human review for high-risk items. we can include redaction pass/fail as part of format conformance.
[03:29] Priya: about regression tests — we want to ensure model upgrades don't degrade on key prompt sets. do you support automated regression test harness?
[03:35] Marcus: yes, Redwood provides a regression harness. we'll store baseline outputs and run nightly or on-deploy comparisons using diffs and scoring. for this POC we'll run baseline vs current model and a second run after any tuning.
[03:47] Tom: sample payloads: our outputs are JSON with fields {summary, severity, codes}. can you validate schema enforcement?
[03:54] Marcus: yes, schema validation is part of the pipeline — we do strict JSON schema checks and can fail the prompt if format is off. sometimes transcriptions have slight variations, we also support structured output/tuples to minimize free text.
[04:08] Priya: what about hallucination detection automation? it's tricky.
[04:12] Marcus: agree. automated heuristics + ground-truth checks for known facts — for open-ended items we combine LLM-based contradiction checks and human sampling. for clinical facts we'll compare against your reference dataset.
[04:27] Sofia: let's outline the benchmarks we will run during the POC: baseline latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput at target QPS for your peak, golden prompt correctness, hallucination rate, format conformance, and regression drift.
[04:40] Marcus: plus cost per token estimates for hosted vs dedicated and the impact of batching/kv cache. we'll include quantization variants if you want to test lower-cost profiles.
[04:50] Tom: yes, we want cost comparisons. also curious about caching — KV cache caching?
[04:55] Marcus: KV cache — apologies, KV cache — it'll help for prefix-heavy workloads like multi-turn triage. we can simulate typical conversation lengths and measure token savings.
[05:05] Priya: timeline detail — you said 4 weeks earlier. can you map deliverables by week?
[05:09] Marcus: Week 0 (setup & infra): 3 days to provision test tenant, set up service accounts, VPC peering if private, and ingest initial golden prompts. Week 1 (baseline perf): load tests + p95 numbers. Week 2 (quality eval): run golden prompts, hallucination checks, regression harness. Week 3 (analysis & tuning): iterate, retest, final report and recommendations. We'll send a detailed schedule in the SOW.
[05:33] Tom: what's needed on our side for Week 0?
[05:36] Marcus: service account, sample payloads, golden prompts, expected output schema, and network details if Private. If hosted we'll just need API keys and sample data.
[05:47] Linda: on compliance — we need KMS integration and audit logs preserved for the POC. can Redwood provide that?
[05:53] Marcus: yes, for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS and extensive audit logs. for hosted we provide audit logs and optional integrations; we can detail exact retention windows in the SOW.
[06:04] Priya: success criteria recap?
[06:07] Sofia: golden prompts >=90%, regression F1 drop <3%, hallucination <2%, format errors <1%, latency p95 targets per deployment. If we hit all of these we consider POC successful and move to Dedicated proposal.
[06:21] Tom: sounds good. one more thing — benchmarking environment parity. we want tests to run against similar GPU types to our eventual Dedicated plan. can you match GPU family?
[06:30] Marcus: we usually map to A100/RTX equivalents depending on availability; specify preferred instance family and we'll attempt parity. we will also provide equivalent perf profiles for hosted options.
[06:40] Priya: scoring mechanics — can you share the notebook you mentioned?
[06:44] Marcus: yes we'll attach a scoring notebook and a small script to compute composite scores, plus a dashboard prototype showing per-prompt failures.
[06:52] Sofia: what about regression gating? if a model upgrade reduces score by >3% do we block?
[06:58] Priya: we want a guardrail: auto-block on major degradations for clinical-critical prompts, and alert + canary for minor regressions.
[07:07] Marcus: we can set canary rollout policies and automatic fallback to previous model variant on regression beyond threshold. that's standard in Redwood's rollout tooling.
[07:16] Tom: dataset size for regression: you said 1k random samples. is that 1k per day or total?
[07:21] Marcus: total sample for regression snapshot. we can run larger sample sets for more statistical power if you like.
[07:28] Linda: about PII — are transcripts preserved? what's redaction policy?
[07:33] Marcus: retention is configurable; for POC we can set short retention and disable logs in hosted if needed. for Dedicated/Private you control retention and KMS. we'll include that in the SOW.
[07:43] Sofia: ok let's go through the evaluation specifics quickly — Golden prompt design: you provide 200 prompts split across intent buckets, edge cases, and PHI tests. We'll label ground truth and expected structured output for each. Reg tests: baseline outputs stored; diff and compute F1 + BLEU for summarization tasks. Hallucination checks: entity-level comparisons, contradiction detection, and human review of flagged items. Format: strict JSON schema checks.
[08:10] Priya: for scoring, accuracy 50% weight is fine. for hallucination we want a stricter multiplier for clinical-critical prompts — maybe double penalty. can that be configured?
[08:19] Marcus: yes we support weighted buckets where certain prompts are high-priority and apply higher penalties. we'll add that to the scoring notebook.
[08:26] Tom: what about false positives on hallucination detection? automated heuristics sometimes flag correct but paraphrased content.
[08:33] Marcus: true, that's why we combine automated checks with a human-in-the-loop sample: we set thresholds to avoid noisy auto-blocking and use manual review for edge cases.
[08:43] Sofia: any other concerns?
[08:45] Linda: just need to review the SOC2 docs and encryption details. we'll send a list of compliance Qs.
[08:51] Sofia: noted. we'll include those items in the SOW.
[08:54] Marcus: quick note on benchmarks: we'll run both cold-start and warm (with KV cache primed) scenarios, measure token-cost and latency tradeoffs, and provide recommendations on batching/quantization.
[09:05] Tom: can you run a cost model? we want a per-req cost estimate at 10k/day and 25k/day.
[09:10] Marcus: yes we'll include cost models for hosted vs dedicated with assumed batch sizes.
[09:15] Priya: closing — timeline again and responsibilities?
[09:19] Sofia: I'll send SOW + benchmark template by 2026-04-17. Marcus will provision the tenant and run initial perf tests by 2026-04-20. Tom to send prompts and schemas by 2026-04-22. Linda to send compliance questions by 2026-04-21.
[09:32] Priya: ok let's wrap. thanks all, looking forward to seeing the SOW and getting started.
[09:36] Sofia: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the infra kick-off. bye.
[44:30] End of recording (approx)
notes: Redwood to provide scoring notebook and regression harness.
Customer to provide 200 golden prompts and sample output schema.
